title: Kestrel carry system product page
audience: Urban commuters comparing a durable modular daypack
scenario: Kestrel sells one 22-liter pack with three included modules and two color options.
task: Build a static commerce product detail page that supports confident product evaluation without pretending to complete a purchase.

sections: Store navigation with Packs, Modules, Repair, Field notes, and Cart (0)
Product summary for Kestrel 22L at $189 with Slate and Lichen options
Static product gallery with four labeled views
Included modules: laptop sleeve, cable pouch, and bottle cradle
Specification list covering 22 L capacity, 980 g weight, and 46 × 30 × 16 cm size
Shipping note, returns note, and footer

requirements: Use a fieldset and legend or equivalent semantics for the two color options
Label the static Add to cart control as a demonstrative non-working state
Expose gallery view labels and useful image alternatives
Keep price, included items, specifications, and policies easy to locate
Handle the specification table and gallery labels at narrow widths
constraints: Do not implement checkout, inventory, image zoom, or cart mutations
Do not add sale pricing, reviews, ratings, or sustainability certifications
Do not use remote product photography
Do not obscure the fact that this is a static demonstration
evaluation_focus: Honest static representation of commerce controls
Decision-supporting hierarchy and product detail completeness
